Name: Bulleh Shah
Description: Renowned Punjabi Sufi poet known for spiritual poetry

Name: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
Description: Great Sindhi Sufi poet and mystic

Name: Sultan Bahoo
Description: Major Punjabi Sufi poet and saint

Name: Sachal Sarmast
Description: Sindhi mystic poet known for multilingual poetry

Name: Lal Shahbaz Qalandar
Description: One of the most famous Sufi saints of South Asia

Name: Khushal Khan Khattak
Description: Pashtun warrior-poet and tribal chief of the Khattak tribe, regarded as one of the major figures of Pashto literature; his poetry promoted Pashtun unity and resistance to Mughal rule.

Name: Waris Shah
Description: Punjabi Sufi poet of the Chishti order, renowned for his epic retelling of the tragic romance of Heer and Ranjha, one of the most celebrated works in Punjabi literature.

Name: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
Description: Persian Sufi scholar and saint; author of Kashf al-Mahjub, the earliest known Persian treatise on Sufism. Revered as the patron saint of Lahore, his shrine (Data Darbar) is one of South Asia's most visited.

Name: Abdul Hameed Baba
Description: Pashtun Sufi poet from the village of Mashogagar near Peshawar, known for morally-themed verse reflecting on the transience of the world, rooted in Sufi thought.

Name: Jam Durrak
Famous_Work: Balochi ghazals; Balochi verse adaptations of Shirin-Farhad and Laila-Majnun
Description: Chief court poet of Nasir Khan I of Kalat (r. 1749-1794); regarded as the earliest named poet of Balochi literature and credited with introducing the ghazal form to Balochi verse. Exact birth/death years are not firmly documented in historical sources.
